description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
readmeExcerpt:
ADHD-friendly outputs. No ADHD diagnosis needed!

🇬🇧 · 🇨🇳 · 🇪🇸 · 🇧🇷 · 🇯🇵 · 🇻🇳 · 🇰🇷 · 🇮🇷 · 🇹🇭 · 🇸🇦

## Install Copy/paste into your CLI prompt: ```text Install the i-have-adhd skill/plugin from https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd, refer to the repo's AGENTS.md for instructions. ``` Or 🔗 [check the installation instructions](INSTALL.md). ## What it does A skill for your coding assistant that stops it from burying the answer. Action first. Steps numbered. No "Hope this helps!" [Kacper Rutkiewicz | AI Made Simple](https://youtu.be/NEl8kPWZP_Y) has made a good breakdown of an earlier version of the skill. ## What changes
## Before > Great question! Let me think about this. Your auth flow has a few moving pieces: the middleware, the token verification, and the cookie handling. Looking at `src/auth.ts`, the `verifyToken` function (around lines 42-58) seems to be using an older `jsonwebtoken` API. One approach would be to update the package and rewrite that function. After making the change, you'd want to run the auth tests to confirm nothing breaks. By the way, you might also want to look at your dependency versions overall. Hope this helps! Let me know if you want to dig deeper. ## After > Edit `src/auth.ts:42` to update the token validation. > > 1. Open `src/auth.ts` > 2. Replace `verifyToken` (lines 42–58) with the snippet below > 3. Run `npm test -- auth.spec.ts` > > Next: paste the first failing line if any test fails.
## The rules 10 rules. Full text in [SKILL.md](./skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md). 1. Lead with the next action. 2. Number multi-step tasks. 3. End with one concrete next step. 4. Suppress tangents. 5. Restate state every turn. 6. Specific time estimates (minutes, not "a bit"). 7. Make wins visible. 8. Matter-of-fact errors. 9. Cap lists to 5 items. 10. No preamble. No recap. No closers. ## Tune it Fork, edit `skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md`, then swap your copy in: ```bash claude plugin uninstall i-have-adhd # drop the upstream copy first: claude plugin marketplace remove i-have-adhd # fork and upstream share both names claude plugin marketplace add /i-have-adhd claude plugin install i-have-adhd@i-have-adhd ``` Restart your coding assistant, then re-invoke `/i-have-adhd`. ## Credits Loosely based on *The Adult ADHD Tool Kit* by J. Russell Ramsay and Anthony L. Rostain. Adapted for how an LLM should respond, not how a human should organize their day. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Star ⭐ if it saved you one scroll past one "Great question!"

ADHD-friendly outputs. No ADHD diagnosis needed!

🇬🇧 · 🇨🇳 · 🇪🇸 · 🇧🇷 · 🇯🇵 · 🇻🇳 · 🇰🇷 · 🇮🇷 · 🇹🇭 · 🇸🇦

Install

Copy/paste into your CLI prompt:

Install the i-have-adhd skill/plugin from https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd, refer to the repo's AGENTS.md for instructions.

Or 🔗 check the installation instructions.

What it does

A skill for your coding assistant that stops it from burying the answer. Action first. Steps numbered. No "Hope this helps!"

Kacper Rutkiewicz | AI Made Simple has made a good breakdown of an earlier version of the skill.

What changes

Before

Great question! Let me think about this. Your auth flow has a few moving pieces: the middleware, the token verification, and the cookie handling. Looking at src/auth.ts, the verifyToken function (around lines 42-58) seems to be using an older jsonwebtoken API. One approach would be to update the package and rewrite that function. After making the change, you'd want to run the auth tests to confirm nothing breaks. By the way, you might also want to look at your dependency versions overall. Hope this helps! Let me know if you want to dig deeper.

After

Edit src/auth.ts:42 to update the token validation.

  1. Open src/auth.ts
  2. Replace verifyToken (lines 42–58) with the snippet below
  3. Run npm test -- auth.spec.ts

Next: paste the first failing line if any test fails.

The rules

10 rules. Full text in SKILL.md.

  1. Lead with the next action.
  2. Number multi-step tasks.
  3. End with one concrete next step.
  4. Suppress tangents.
  5. Restate state every turn.
  6. Specific time estimates (minutes, not "a bit").
  7. Make wins visible.
  8. Matter-of-fact errors.
  9. Cap lists to 5 items.
  10. No preamble. No recap. No closers.

Tune it

Fork, edit skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md, then swap your copy in:

claude plugin uninstall i-have-adhd            # drop the upstream copy first:
claude plugin marketplace remove i-have-adhd   # fork and upstream share both names
claude plugin marketplace add <your-username>/i-have-adhd
claude plugin install i-have-adhd@i-have-adhd

Restart your coding assistant, then re-invoke /i-have-adhd.

Credits

Loosely based on The Adult ADHD Tool Kit by J. Russell Ramsay and Anthony L. Rostain. Adapted for how an LLM should respond, not how a human should organize their day.

License

MIT.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A plugin that forces AI coding assistants to produce step-by-step, actionable, and ADHD-friendly outputs.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository provides a specialized skill plugin designed to modify the output of AI coding assistants like Claude Code to be more accessible for neurodivergent users. Instead of returning dense paragraphs or complex monolithic code blocks, the tool forces the AI to provide step-by-step, highly actionable outputs. It achieves this by injecting context-aware formatting prompts that suppress conversational boilerplate and prioritize task decomposition. By reducing cognitive load and decision paralysis, it creates a more structured and less overwhelming interaction loop for developers. It is completely localized for seamless installation directly into the AI tool.
keyFeatures: Output formatting: Forces AI assistants to deliver solutions in small, digestible chunks rather than overwhelming monolithic blocks.
Boilerplate suppression: Instructs the AI to omit unnecessary conversational filler and focus purely on actionable code changes.
Task decomposition: Automatically guides the AI to break down large feature requests into manageable, step-by-step sub-tasks.
Cross-agent compatibility: Provides installation instructions and plugins for various coding environments including Claude and Codex.
Implicit invocation: Can be configured to automatically apply formatting when the AI detects tasks that benefit from structured output.

useCases.title: Overcoming decision paralysis
useCases.description: Neurodivergent developers can tackle large refactoring tasks without getting overwhelmed by excessive, unstructured information.

useCases.title: Step-by-step implementation
useCases.description: Users can execute complex architectural changes sequentially, ensuring each small piece is verified before moving to the next.

useCases.title: Reducing conversational noise
useCases.description: Engineers seeking rapid answers can strip away polite filler text from their AI assistant to focus solely on the necessary code.

useCases.title: Structured learning
useCases.description: Beginners can use the step-by-step outputs to better understand the logic behind complex code generation.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers with ADHD or anyone who finds standard AI coding assistant outputs overwhelming and dense. It is designed for those who prefer highly structured, actionable, and step-by-step communication.
